Evaluation status | Only what waits for you, or what you finished | No | «Waiting for your evaluation» or «Evaluated»

Workflow
This page owns the manager's stage of the cycle (the whole cycle, with its stages and dates, is in the page «Evaluation cycle»).
1. HR opens the cycle and the employees send their self-evaluations. When someone sends theirs, you are notified («A self-evaluation is waiting for your review») and the notice box names them.
2. HR moves the cycle to the manager's stage; you are notified that it began. Before that, the buttons are dimmed and explain why.
3. As the direct manager: you press «Evaluate», enter the results scores, rate the behaviours with notes, tick the catalog items you accept, watch the live score, then «Save draft» and «Send the evaluation».
4. At your first send the upper manager is notified («An evaluation is waiting for your review»). The evaluation of an indirect report cannot be written before their direct manager sent (the button says «Waiting for the review of <manager> (their direct manager) first»).
5. As the upper manager: you open the evaluation the direct manager sent, review it, change it if needed and send. Each of you keeps your own copy: what the direct manager entered is never lost. If the upper manager's copy has been sent, its score is the one calibrated; a draft that was not sent does not count, and the direct manager's sent score is used instead.
6. The scores then go to calibration (the page «Calibration and approval»). After the manager's stage is over the evaluation is read only.
7. Return after an objection: if the approver accepts an objection of one of your people, their evaluation comes back to you as a draft and you are notified. You (the direct manager) revise and send, then the upper manager reviews and sends again. This is the only time an evaluation is editable after the manager's stage.
8. Milestones can be recorded for each member during the cycle, apart from the stages.
Status / Stage | Meaning | Who can move it (permission key) | Moves to
Not started | You wrote nothing for this person | You: Evaluate team members and send the evaluation | Draft
Draft | A form you saved and did not send | You: Evaluate team members and send the evaluation | Sent
Sent | Your evaluation was sent (you may save a change until the manager's stage ends) | You: Evaluate team members and send the evaluation; the next reader is the upper manager, then calibration | Read only after the manager's stage (back to Draft only by an accepted objection)
Blocked: the cycle is not open | No cycle | HR: Open the evaluation cycle, move it on and change its dates (open it) | Blocked: stage not started
Blocked: the manager's stage has not started | The cycle is still in self-evaluation | HR: Open the evaluation cycle, move it on and change its dates | Open to write
Blocked: waiting for the direct manager | The upper manager before the direct manager sent | The direct manager: Evaluate team members and send the evaluation | Open to write
Blocked: the manager's stage is over | Read only | — | —
Milestone: Not recorded / Recorded / Recorded and read by the employee / Does not run this year | The state of each milestone of the member | You: Record the minutes of a milestone for a team member; the employee ticks Acknowledge reading the minutes of my milestone | Recorded, then read; recording again clears the employee's tick
Automatic things
- Notices to you: the manager's stage began; a self-evaluation is waiting; an evaluation came back after an objection. Notices from you: the upper manager at the direct manager's first send; the employee when you record minutes of a milestone.
- Reminders (HR sets them in «Evaluation cycle»): every N days while evaluations wait for you in the manager's stage, and N days before a milestone date when the minutes are missing; they stop when the work is done and are never sent on Friday or Saturday.
- Audit: drafts, sends and changes of evaluations and the recording and reading of minutes are recorded.
What each person sees: you see your unit and below («unit and below» by default), in two scopes (direct reports only, or everyone below); a person outside it does not exist for you. The employee sees no score before approval and the individual notification; they see the minutes of their milestones and tick that they read them.

Business rules
- Who evaluates whom (FR-120): every manager evaluates everyone below them, direct and indirect, at every level.
- One chain: the employee evaluates themselves, the direct manager reviews and adjusts, the upper manager reviews and may change the direct manager's evaluation, then calibration and approval. An indirect report cannot be evaluated before their direct manager's review.
- Why a button may be blocked (always shown with its reason): the cycle is not open yet; the manager's stage has not started (the current stage is named); waiting for the direct manager's review first; the manager's stage is over (read only). Only when an employee's evaluation is returned after an accepted objection can it be edited again.
- Scoring: results are scored from 0 to 100 per criterion; behaviours use Always = 100, Often = 75, Sometimes = 50, Rarely = 25, Never = 0, and the average is taken. Basic = results × their weight + behaviour × theirs (the weights belong to the development stage of the employee, for example 60/40 for Foundation). Then learning (approved learning hours against the hours of the stage, up to 10 points), internal initiatives and contribution to growth (each up to its cap) are added. The final score never goes above the cap of the stage (for example 125 for Foundation) (FR-121).
- Grade scale: exceptional from 110, exceeds expectations 95 to 109.9, meets expectations 80 to 94.9, needs improvement 65 to 79.9, below expectations under 65.
- Behaviour notes: required at Always, Rarely and Never, at least 5 characters, for both employee and manager.
- The sent button stays off while a field is invalid; the server refuses an evaluation with wrong fields or when the stage is over.
- The employee's self-evaluation does not bind the manager.
- Milestones are a fixed calendar: short reviews on 15 January and 15 July, pulses on 15 March and 15 September, and the warning grade in October that does not run this year; their dates can be changed by HR in the evaluation cycle page. The minutes carry no scores. Recording them again clears the employee's acknowledgement.
- Reminders: the manager is reminded every N days of the evaluations waiting for them, and of milestones whose minutes are not recorded; reminders stop once the work is done and are never sent on Friday or Saturday.
- Like every list the page has search, filters, the table / cards switch and export.

Tips and common problems
- The button is dimmed: click it and read the reason, it is one of the blocks above.
- A person of your team is missing: they are outside your unit and below, or have no evaluation in this cycle («Nobody in your team has an evaluation in this cycle»).
- The send failed: check the fields (scores from 0 to 100, notes where required) and that the manager's stage is still on.

title: My tasks
text:
«My tasks» is one place for everything you have to do, everything you asked others to do, and everything you follow. A manager also sees a tab for the team. The same list can be shown as a table, as cards, or as a Kanban board with one column per status. The matrix, a small summary of your open tasks in four squares, sits on the home page.

Who sees it
- View permission: View my tasks and task details («View my tasks and task details»). Default scope: own (the tasks you are linked to).
- Default roles: the Employee role holds it, together with create, edit and change-status for your own tasks. The «my team» tab needs View the team tasks page («View the team tasks page»), which the head role of every unit holds (unit and below).
- The page does not need platform admin mode. An administrator can hide it for a role from the page visibility screen.
- A task you have no relation to, or that is outside your scope, is shown as «not found».

What you can do
Action | What happens | Permission
New task | Opens a popup to create a task | Create a task
Assign to someone else | Choose another person in the «Assigned to» field | Assign a task to another person
Open my team tab | Shows the tasks of direct reports or of everyone below you | View the team tasks page
Matrix on the home page | Your open tasks in four squares | View the task matrix
Edit a task | Changes title, details, due date, priority | Edit a task
Move a task (drag or menu) | Changes the status of your own task | Change the status of my tasks
Move a team task | Changes the status of a team member's task | Change the status of team tasks
Approve / Reject | Decides on a task a person gave to themselves | Approve a self-assigned task / Reject a self-assigned task
Review (accept or send back) | Accepts finished work or returns it with a note | Review the completion of a task (accept or send back)
Reopen | Brings a finished task back | Reopen a finished task
Resubmit | Sends a rejected task for approval again | Resubmit a rejected task for approval
Object | Objects to a task given to you | Object to a task given to me
Follow / Unfollow | Adds the task to your «Following» tab; the button is not shown on a task given to you (it is under «Assigned to me»), because following is for tasks that are not yours | Follow a task
«Add followers» (task page) | You pick a colleague of your company (search from the first letter): they follow the task, see it under «Following» and get a notice, and can stop following by themselves; an icon beside each follower removes them. For the task's assignee, the person who gave it, and a manager whose scope reaches the assignee | Add followers to a task and remove them
Log time | Records time worked | Log time on a task
Archived filter | Shows archived tasks | View archived tasks
Restore | Brings an archived task back | Restore an archived task
Export | Exports the list to a file (scope, columns, file type) | Export task lists
The list has no import: tasks are created one by one, not from a file.

How to
Create a task
1. Click New task.
2. Write the title (required) and the details.
3. Choose the person (you, by default), the tag, the due date (required, not in the past), the priority, the expected time in hours, and repetition (none, daily, weekly, monthly, with an optional end date).
4. Turn on «Mark as urgent» or «Needs review» if needed.
5. Read the line under the form: if the task is for yourself it says who approves it, or that no approval is needed. Click Create task.
Change the status of a task
1. On the board, drag the card to another column using its handle, or open the task and use «Move to».
2. If a note or a completion date is needed, a small window asks for it.
3. If the move is not allowed, the card goes back and the reason is shown.
Follow my team
1. Open the My team tab.
2. Choose «My direct reports» or «Everyone under me».
3. On the board tick «One row per person» to split the board by person.
Find a task
1. Type in the search box: title or task number (TSK-000123).
2. Use the filters: status, priority, person, tag, stale only, overdue only, include finished and rejected, archived.
3. Group the table by due date, status or person, and switch between table, cards and board. The page remembers your choice.

Fields (form inputs)
New task (button New task; the same fields, except «Assign to», the tag and the repetition, appear in «Edit the task»)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Title | A short name of the work; it is what people see in lists, cards and notices. | Yes | 1 to 200 characters.
Details | The full description of what must be done. | No | Up to 5000 characters.
Assign to | Who must do the task. Left on yourself, the task is «for yourself» and goes to your direct manager for approval (a line under the form says who approves, or that nobody does). Another person gets the task at once as «To do» and is notified. | No (yourself by default) | Only people you may give a task to: a manager to anyone under them, an employee to the manager of their department, people on the same ticket to each other, anyone to themselves (needs Assign a task to another person for others).
Tag | The tag of the task (for example «Reports» or «Meetings»). It also decides which colleagues may join the task conversation (see Task details and conversation). | No («No tag») | Active tags of your unit and of the units above it; if your unit has none, the field says so.
Due date | The day the work is due. It drives the reminder, the «Overdue» and «Urgent» marks and the matrix. | Yes (today by default) | A date, not in the past when creating.
Priority | How important the task is; «High» makes it «important» in the matrix. | No | Low, Medium (default), High.
Expected time (hours) | The estimate of the work. When the time logged passes it, the assignee and the person who gave the task are told once. | No | A number above 0, steps of 0.25 hour; empty when unknown.
Repeats | Makes the system create the next task by itself when this one is closed (daily, weekly, monthly). | No | Does not repeat (default), Every day, Every week, Every month.
Repeats until | The last date a repeating task may repeat. Shown only when «Repeats» is not «Does not repeat». | No | A date not before the due date; empty = no end.
Urgent / «Mark as urgent» | Marks the task urgent by hand, whatever its due date. | No | On / Off (default Off).
Personal task | A task for you alone: it starts «To do» at once with no approval, no review and no followers, and your manager does not see it anywhere (no team, matrix or digest). You edit, move, delete and log time on it like any task. When on, «Assign to» and the review option disappear. It shows a «Personal» badge and the list can be narrowed with «Personal only». | No | On / Off (default Off).
Review / «Needs a review» | The assignee cannot finish the task alone: finishing sends it to «Awaiting review» and the reviewer closes it. The reviewer is the person who gave the task (for a task you gave yourself, your approving manager). | No | On / Off (default Off).
There is no attachment field on a task: files are added in the task conversation (see Task details and conversation).
Window «Send the work back» (moving a task from «Awaiting review» to «In progress»)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Note | What is missing; the assignee is notified and sees the note in the history. | Yes | Up to 5000 characters.
Window «When did the work end?» (finishing a task more than the allowed days after its due date)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Completion date | The real day the work ended. | Yes | A date up to today, and not further back than the «Back-dating allowed» days of the task policies (7 by default).

Workflow
What happens when someone creates and assigns a task
1. The creator clicks New task, fills the form and clicks Create the task. The task gets a number such as TSK-000123 and the first line of its history, «Created».
2. Given to another person: the task starts as «To do» at once. The assignee receives the notice «New task». If «Needs a review» is on, the reviewer is the creator.
3. Given to yourself, with a manager: the task starts as «Pending approval» and the manager receives «Approval requested». The manager opens the task and clicks Approve (Approve a self-assigned task; the automatic «Direct manager» role holds it, so everyone with direct reports sees it unless an administrator removes it from the role) or Reject (Reject a self-assigned task), with an optional note. Approving makes it «To do»; rejecting makes it «Rejected». The creator is notified of the decision.
4. Rejected: the owner edits the task and clicks Send again (Resubmit a rejected task for approval); it goes back to the manager as «Pending approval». Given to yourself, with no manager: nobody has to approve, the task is «To do» at once, and the review switch has no effect because there is nobody to review.
5. Objection: while the task is «To do», an assignee who got it from someone else may click Object and choose a reason. The person who gave the task answers: keep it with the assignee, or accept and give it to someone else (who is notified). Unanswered, the objection lapses after 3 working days by default (set in Task policies).
6. Start and work: the assignee (or a manager of the team) moves the task to «In progress» by dragging the card or with «Move to». The assignee logs the time worked with Log time.
7. Finish: the assignee moves the task to «Done». If the task needs a review it goes to «Awaiting review» and the reviewer is notified. If the task is late beyond the allowed days, the window «When did the work end?» asks for the real day.
8. Review: the reviewer accepts (the task becomes «Done») or sends it back to «In progress» with a required note; the assignee is notified.
9. After closing: the person who gave the task, or a manager, may reopen a «Done» task. A repeating task creates the next one when it is closed. A standalone task is archived 30 days after it closes by default (set in Task policies), and Restore brings it back in its earlier status.
Status | Meaning | Who can move it (permission key) | Moves to
Pending approval | A task given to yourself waits for your manager. | The approver: Approve a self-assigned task / Reject a self-assigned task (never by dragging). | To do (approved) or Rejected.
To do | Accepted, not started. | The assignee: Change the status of my tasks; a manager of the team: Change the status of team tasks. | In progress.
In progress | The work is being done. | The assignee: Change the status of my tasks; a manager of the team: Change the status of team tasks. | Done, or Awaiting review if the task needs a review.
Awaiting review | The work is finished and waits for the reviewer. | The reviewer only: Review the completion of a task (accept or send back). | Done, or In progress (note required).
Done | Finished. | The person who gave the task or a manager: Reopen a finished task. | To do, In progress, or Awaiting review (a task that needs review).
Rejected | Refused at approval. | The owner: Resubmit a rejected task for approval (Send again). | Pending approval (or To do when there is no manager).
Automatic things
- Reminder: every morning (6:00 Riyadh time) the assignee receives one reminder the number of days before the due date set in the task policies (1 by default).
- Overdue: the assignee and the person who gave the task are told once when the due date passes. The marks «Urgent», «Overdue» and «Stale» are worked out from the data each time, never stored.
- Weekly summary: on the company's summary day (Sunday by default, 8:00) each manager receives the number of overdue tasks of their direct reports.
- Objection time: a scheduled job closes an unanswered objection after the allowed working days and notifies the giver and the assignee.
- Estimate: one notice when the logged time passes the estimate.
- Archive: every morning standalone tasks closed for long enough are archived and the giver is notified.
- Notices and audit: assigning, approving, rejecting, status changes, objections and archiving create notices (e-mail only for the important ones, never with the title) and are recorded in the audit log and in the history of the task.
What each person sees: the assignee sees the task under «Assigned to me»; the person who gave it under «Assigned by me»; a follower under «Following»; a manager sees their team's tasks under «My team» (within the scope of the key); the approver sees a pending task in their lists. A colleague with an open task in the same tag or a mentioned person sees only the number, title and conversation.

Business rules
- The page opens on open tasks, ordered by due date. Finished and rejected tasks appear only if you tick «Include finished and rejected» (the board always shows every column).
- Tabs: Assigned to me, Assigned by me, Following, and My team for managers. (FR-48)
- Statuses: Pending approval, To do, In progress, Awaiting review, Done, Rejected. A task has a number such as TSK-000123.
- Who may assign to whom: a manager to anyone under them; an employee to the manager of their department; people working on the same ticket to each other; anyone to themselves. (FR-48)
- Self-approval: a task you give to yourself starts as «Pending approval» and is approved or rejected by your direct manager. A person with no manager is approved automatically. An approved task becomes «To do». A rejected task is shown as «Rejected»; its owner edits it and presses Resubmit, and it goes back to the manager. (FR-51)
- Allowed moves:
From | To | Who
Pending approval | any | nobody by dragging; only the approver's decision moves it
To do | In progress | the assignee, or a manager of the team
In progress | Done | the assignee or a manager; if the task needs review it goes to «Awaiting review» instead
Awaiting review | Done | the reviewer only
Awaiting review | In progress | the reviewer only, with a required note
Done | To do / In progress / Awaiting review | whoever assigned the task, or a manager (reopening)
Rejected | any | nobody; resubmit instead
  The reviewer is the person who gave the task (for a self task, the one who approved it). (FR-50)
- Late completion: if a task is finished more than 7 days after its due date, you must give the real completion date. Back-dating is limited to 7 days (the number is set in the task policies). (FR-50)
- Objection: the assignee of a task that someone else gave them may object while it is still «To do», choosing one reason: not my responsibility, not enough time, missing information, conflicting priorities. The task shows an «Objected» mark. The person who gave the task answers: reject (the task stays with the assignee) or accept and give it to someone else. An objection nobody answers lapses after 3 working days (Friday and Saturday are off) and the task stays with the assignee. (FR-52)
- Time log: minutes worked on a day, back-dating up to 7 days. When logged time passes the estimate, the assignee and the person who gave the task are notified once. (FR-48, FR-56)
- Marks: *Urgent* (marked by hand, due within 2 days, or overdue), *Overdue*, *Stale* (no movement for 30 days; not for tasks waiting for approval), *Objected*. Each mark has an icon and text. (FR-49)
- Reminders: a reminder the day before the due date; every Sunday morning each manager receives the overdue tasks of their team; recurring tasks create the next one when the current one is closed. (FR-53)
- Archive: a standalone task is archived 30 days after it closes and leaves the normal lists. Users with the archive key see it with the «Archived» filter and can Restore it; it returns in its earlier status and the assigner is notified. (FR-53)
- Notifications: the assignee is told when a task is assigned; the person who gave the task is told of every status change; the reviewer when a task awaits review; objections and their answers. Nobody is notified of their own change, and quick changes within a minute arrive as one notice. E-mail is sent only for the important ones and never contains the title. (FR-56)
- When an employee leaves, their open tasks go to their direct manager. (FR-55)
- Changes to a task made by two people at once are refused for the second person, who must reload and try again.

Tips / common problems
- A task you expect is missing: check the tab, and tick «Include finished and rejected».
- You cannot drag a card: the card is waiting for approval, rejected, or the move is not yours; the reason is shown when you try.
- You do not see the «My team» tab: you have no team permission or no one reports to you.
- The matrix on the home page counts a task as important if its priority is high and urgent if it is due soon, overdue or marked urgent.

title: Task details and conversation
text:
Click any task in the list to open its page. The page shows what the task is, who is involved, the buttons you may use at this moment, the task conversation, and a button that opens the history of everything that happened to the task as a table. The conversation holds comments, replies, files and mentions of colleagues with @.

Who sees it
- View permission: View my tasks and task details («View my tasks and task details»), scope own. You need to be related to the task: assignee, the person who gave it, approver, reviewer, follower, or a manager whose team includes the assignee.
- The conversation needs Read the comments of a task («Read the comments of a task»). The Employee role holds all the comment keys except «delete anybody's comment» and the comment rules.
- A task outside your reach is shown as «not found».
- A colleague who has an open task in the same category, or a person mentioned with @, sees only the task number, title and conversation, nothing else.

What you can do
Action | What happens | Permission
Edit | Changes title, details, due date, priority | Edit a task
Move to | Changes the status, only to statuses allowed to you | Change the status of my tasks / Change the status of team tasks
Approve / Reject | Decides on a pending self task | Approve a self-assigned task / Reject a self-assigned task
Resubmit | Sends a rejected task back for approval | Resubmit a rejected task for approval
Object | Objects to a task given to you | Object to a task given to me
Answer the objection | Rejects it or gives the task to someone else | the person who gave the task
Log time | Records hours and minutes worked on a day | Log time on a task
Follow / Unfollow | Starts or stops notices about the task | Follow a task
Add followers | Opens a window to add followers to the task and remove them | Add followers to a task and remove them
Restore | Brings an archived task back | Restore an archived task
Delete | Hides the task (and its conversation) from everyone after a confirmation; the record stays in the database and the audit log says who deleted it. Offered to its giver, and to a person whose scope reaches the assignee | Delete a task (hidden from everyone, its record is kept) (Delete a task); not held by the «Employee» role, held by the head role of every unit for its unit and below
Write a comment | Adds a comment to the conversation | Write a comment on a task
Reply | Answers a comment | Reply to a comment on a task
Attach files | Adds files to a comment | Attach files to a comment
Mention with @ | Names a colleague | Mention a colleague with @ in a comment
Edit my comment | Changes your own comment | Edit my comment
Delete my comment | Removes your own comment | Delete my comment
Delete anyone's comment | Removes someone else's comment | Delete anybody’s comment (Delete anybody's comment)
Only the buttons you may use are shown.

How to
Write a comment
1. Open the task and go to the «Comments» section.
2. Write in the «Write a comment» box. Press Ctrl+Enter to send.
3. To mention a colleague type @ and pick the name from the list.
4. To attach files, use the attach box under the text (up to 5 files per comment by default). Click Send.
Reply to a comment
1. Click the reply icon on the comment.
2. Write your answer under it and click Send. Replies go one level only: a reply is shown under the comment it answers.
Edit or delete your comment
1. Use the pencil or the bin icon on your comment.
2. For deletion, confirm. The text and files disappear for everyone, a line «This comment was deleted» stays, and the replies under it stay too.
Log time or object
1. Click Log time, enter the hours, the minutes and the working day, then confirm.
2. Or click Object, choose the reason, add an optional note and send.

Fields (form inputs)
Edit the task (button Edit, Edit a task; status is never edited here, it only moves by the table of moves)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Title | The name of the task. | Yes | 1 to 200 characters.
Details | The description. | No | Up to 5000 characters.
Due date | A new due date; it restarts the reminder. | Yes | A date; an edited task may keep an earlier date.
Priority | Importance (feeds the matrix). | No | Low, Medium, High.
Expected time (hours) | The estimate. | No | A number above 0, steps of 0.25 hour.
Urgent / «Mark as urgent» | Manual urgent mark. | No | On / Off.
Review / «Needs a review» | Turns the review step on or off. Turning it on needs somebody to review: the reviewer already named, else the person who gave the task, else the approver. | No | On / Off.
The assignee, the tag and the repetition are not in this window. If two people save at the same time, the second is refused and must reload.
Approve / Reject / Send again (windows «Approve the task», «Reject the task», «Send the task again»)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Note (optional) | A word to the owner about the decision; it is kept in the history for Approve and Reject (Send again does not keep a note). | No | Up to 5000 characters.
Object to the task (button Object)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Reason | Why the task should not stay with you. | Yes | Not my responsibility, Not enough time, Information is missing, Conflicting priorities.
Note (optional) | More explanation for the person who gave the task. | No | Up to 1000 characters.
Answer the objection (button Answer the objection, only the person who gave the task)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Your answer | «I keep the task with its assignee» (reject the objection) or «I accept the objection and give the task to someone else». | Yes | One of the two.
Give the task to | The new assignee, shown only when you accept; the person is told. | Yes, when accepting | Only people you may give a task to, and not the current assignee.
Note (optional) | An explanation of your answer. | No | Up to 1000 characters.
Log time (button Log time, Log time on a task)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Hours | The hours you worked on the task that day. | Yes (at least hours or minutes) | A whole number, 0 or more; with the minutes the total may not pass 24 hours.
Minutes | The rest of the time, in minutes. | No | A whole number from 0 to 59. For longer than an hour, write the hours in their own box.
Day worked | The day the work was done. | Yes | Today or earlier, not further back than the «Back-dating allowed» days of the task policies (7 by default).
If you write more than 24 hours in one entry, a message under the two boxes says a day has only 24 hours and shows what you wrote, and Log stays off; split longer work across the days it was done. If both boxes are empty or zero, a message asks for a time.
Comment box (section «Comments»)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Write a comment | The text of the comment. @ opens the list of colleagues you can mention; a mentioned person is notified and joins the conversation. Writing under «Reply» answers one comment. | Yes, unless a file is attached | Up to 5000 characters. @ only when you hold Mention a colleague with @ in a comment.
Attach files to the comment | Files that go with the comment (the attach box is for new comments and replies, not for edits). | No | Up to the «Most files in a comment» of the task policies (5 by default, at most 10). Images, PDF, Word and Excel; the real type is checked.
Edit your comment | The new text of your own comment. | Yes | Up to 5000 characters; within the edit time of the task policies (15 minutes by default).

Workflow
The task keeps the life described in the «My tasks» page (statuses and moves). This page is where each step is done and recorded.
Steps on the details page
1. Open the task. The banner tells its state: waiting for approval (with the approver's name), open objection (with the lapse date) or archived.
2. The buttons shown are only the ones the API allows now: Approve / Reject for the approver of a pending task; Send again for the owner of a rejected task; Move to for the assignee or a manager; Object and Answer the objection; Log time; Edit; Follow; Restore for an archived task.
3. The View history button (the «History of the task» section at the bottom of the page) opens a window with a table: number, date and time, by (or «The system»), event and details (the two statuses of a status change, the reason of an objection, the minutes logged, the note). Oldest first; anyone who can see the task sees it. Every step adds a line to the history: Created, Edited, Changed status, Approved, Rejected, Sent again, Objected, Objection answered, Objection lapsed, Archived, Restored, Handed over, Given to someone else, Time logged.
4. The conversation: a person with the keys and a relation that allows it writes a comment (with files and @), replies to a comment, and edits or deletes their own comment within the edit time. The people notified are listed under Business rules.
5. When the task is closed and archived, the conversation becomes read-only; the company may also close it some days after the task is done.
Status | Meaning | Who can move it (permission key) | Moves to
Comment: written | A comment or a reply is in the conversation. | The writer: Write a comment on a task / Reply to a comment on a task. | Edited, Deleted.
Comment: edited | The author changed the text; it shows «Edited». | The author: Edit my comment, within the edit time. | Deleted.
Comment: deleted | The text and files are gone for everyone; a line «This comment was deleted» stays, and the replies stay. | The author: Delete my comment; anybody's comment: Delete anybody’s comment. | Final.
Conversation: open | Everyone with a relation that allows it can write. | — | Closed.
Conversation: closed | Read-only. Happens when the task is archived or when the days set in the task policies pass after the task is done. | The system. | —
Automatic things
- Notices: the mentioned person (also by e-mail), the person you reply to, the assignee and the person who gave the task, and followers (once while an earlier notice is unread). Nobody is told of their own comment; e-mail never carries the text.
- Status notices: the person who gave the task and the followers are told of each status change; the reviewer when the task awaits review; the assignee when the work is sent back.
- Time: one notice when the logged time passes the estimate.
- Audit: comments are recorded in the audit log without their text; task steps are recorded with their history line.
What each person sees: the assignee, the person who gave the task, the approver, the reviewer, a follower and a manager of the assignee see the whole page. A colleague with an open task in the same tag, and a person mentioned with @, see only the number, title and conversation.

Business rules
- The page shows: status, priority and marks (urgent, overdue, stale, objected), who gave the task, the reviewer, the approver, logged time against the estimate, repetition, followers, and the history of events (created, edited, status changed, approved, rejected, resubmitted, objection, archived, restored, ownership moved, time logged). (FR-48)
- A banner appears for an archived task, for an open objection (with the date it lapses), and for a task waiting for approval (with the approver's name).
- Who may do what in the conversation is decided by two things together: your role must hold the key of the action, and your relation to the task must be switched on for that action in the company's table («Who does what in task comments», see the Task policies section). You may have several relations at once; one is enough. (FR-66)
- By default the parties of the task (assignee, the person who gave it, approver, reviewer, follower, manager) may do every action. A colleague of the same category and a mentioned person may only read, write and reply.
- Only active employees of the company can be mentioned. A mentioned person joins the conversation as «mentioned»; this does not make them a follower and does not open the task to them.
- You may edit or delete your own comment for 15 minutes after writing it (the number is in the task policies). An edited comment shows «Edited». Deleting someone else's comment needs its own key.
- A comment needs text or at least one file. Text is limited to 5000 characters.
- The conversation stays open after the task is done. When the task is archived it is read-only, and the company may close it some days after the task is closed (0 = never). The page then says «The conversation of this task is closed: you can only read».
- Notices: the mentioned person (also by e-mail), the person you reply to, the assignee and the person who gave the task, and followers (once, while an earlier notice is unread). Nobody is notified of their own comment. E-mail never carries the text of a comment.
- Images, PDF, Word, Excel and CSV open in a window (a CSV as a table); other files download. Word, Excel and CSV files are accepted; the system checks the real file type, not just the name.
- The conversation has no list, so it has no export. Comments are recorded in the audit log without their text. (FR-66)

Tips / common problems
- You can read but cannot write: your role lacks the key, or your relation to the task is switched off for writing. Ask an administrator.
- The edit icon disappeared: the edit time passed.
- You see only the title and the conversation: you are a same-category colleague or were mentioned.

title: Task tags
text:
Every unit keeps its own tags for its tasks, for example «Reports» or «Meetings». A tag is chosen when a task is created (the edit window has no tag field), and tasks can be filtered by it. This page lists the tags and lets authorised people add, edit and delete them.

Who sees it
- View permission: View the task tags page («View the task tags page»). Scopes you can give: own (the person's own unit), unit, unit and below, company, all.
- Default roles: no default role holds it, including the Employee role and the unit head role. An administrator gives it from the permissions page.
- The page does not need platform admin mode. It appears in the menu under Tasks, and can be hidden by page visibility.

What you can do
Action | What happens | Permission
Add a tag | Opens a popup to create a tag | Add a task tag
Edit (row icon, or click the row) | Changes the names or the status (the unit cannot be changed) | Edit a task tag
Delete (row icon) | Deletes the tag after confirmation | Delete a task tag
Export | Exports the list (scope, columns, file type) | Export task lists
Search | Searches the name or the unit | —
Filter by status | Shows only active or only inactive tags | —
Table / cards | Switches the way the list is shown | —
The list has no import: tags are few and are added one by one.

How to
Add a tag
1. Click Add a tag.
2. Write the name in Arabic and the name in English (the English name can be filled in automatically while you type Arabic).
3. Choose the unit the tag belongs to.
4. Keep «Active (shown when tasks are created)» ticked, then save.
Stop using a tag without deleting it
1. Click the row, untick «Active», and save.
2. The tag no longer appears when tasks are created, and old tasks keep it.
Delete a tag
1. Click the delete icon on the row.
2. Read the confirmation «Delete the tag?» and confirm.

Fields (form inputs)
Add a tag / Edit the tag (the dialog keeps the title «Add a tag» or «Edit the tag»; the menu item is «Task tags» and the list column is «Tag»)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Unit | The unit the tag belongs to. Only people of that unit, and the units below it, will be offered the tag when they create tasks. It is chosen only when adding; an existing tag cannot be moved to another unit. | Yes (adding) | One of the units in the scope of your Add a task tag key.
Arabic name | The name shown in Arabic. | Yes | 2 to 120 characters.
English name | The name shown in English; filled in automatically while you type the Arabic name, and you may change it. | Yes | 2 to 120 characters.
Active (offered on new tasks) | Whether people can choose the tag on new tasks. Untick it to stop using the tag without losing it from old tasks. | No | Ticked by default.

Workflow
A tag has a short life, and it works behind the tasks that use it.
1. A person with Add a task tag clicks Add a tag, chooses the unit, writes the two names and saves. The tag is active at once.
2. When someone creates a task, the «Tag» list offers the active tags of their unit and of the units above it. The person chooses one (or none). The tag is also checked again when the task is saved.
3. Colleagues with an open task in the same tag may join the conversation of each other's tasks (reading, writing and replying by default).
4. To retire the tag, a person with Edit a task tag unticks «Active». Old tasks keep it; new tasks no longer offer it.
5. To remove it, a person with Delete a task tag clicks the delete icon and confirms. A tag that tasks use is refused: turn it off instead.
Status | Meaning | Who can move it (permission key) | Moves to
Active | Offered on new tasks. | Edit: Edit a task tag. | Inactive, Deleted.
Inactive | Hidden from new tasks; old tasks keep it. | Edit: Edit a task tag. | Active, Deleted.
Deleted | Removed from the list; allowed only when no task uses it. | Delete: Delete a task tag. | Final.
Automatic things: nothing runs on a schedule. The tag is checked when a task is created or edited (it must be active and belong to a unit of the creator or of the assignee). Adding, editing and deleting a tag are recorded in the audit log.
What each person sees: a person with View the task tags page sees the tags of the units in the scope of the key (own = their own unit). Everyone who creates a task sees, in the form, only the active tags of their unit and above. The tag name appears on the task cards and in the tag filter of the lists.

Business rules
- A tag belongs to one unit only. The New task form offers the active tags of the creator's unit and of the units above it; a tag is accepted when it belongs to such a unit of the creator or of the assignee. (FR-54)
- Both names (Arabic and English) are required.
- Only active tags are offered when creating tasks.
- If tasks use a tag, deactivate it instead of deleting it; the confirmation message says so.
- Your permission scope decides which units' tags you may add, edit or delete: «own» means your own unit; wider scopes reach the units below you, the company, or everything.
- The tags also decide who may see the conversation of a task: a colleague with an open task in the same tag may read, write and reply in that task's conversation (see Task details and conversation).
- Changes are recorded in the audit log.

Tips / common problems
- The tag list is empty when creating a task: your unit and the units above it have no active tag yet. Ask someone with Add a task tag to add one.
- You cannot delete a tag: tasks use it. Turn it off.

title: Task policies
text:
This page holds every number that governs tasks for one company (when a task counts as urgent, when a reminder is sent, how long an objection waits, and so on) and, below them, the table of who may do what in task conversations. Every number has limits, so no value can switch tasks off.

Who sees it
- View permission: View the task policies page («View the task policies page»), scope all.
- Needs platform admin mode: yes. The page appears in the menu only while admin mode is on.
- Default roles: no ordinary role holds it (not the Employee role and not the unit head role); it belongs to the platform administrator. The table of conversation rules needs View the comment rules matrix («View the comment rules matrix»).

What you can do
Action | What happens | Permission
Choose the company | Shows the policies of that company | View the task policies page
Change numbers and Save | Saves all the numbers of the company at once | Edit the task policies
View the conversation table | Shows who may do what in task comments | View the comment rules matrix
Change the conversation table and Save | Saves the whole table at once | Edit the comment rules matrix
Without the edit key the fields can be read but the Save button is not shown.

How to
Change a policy number
1. Turn on platform admin mode.
2. Open Task policies and choose the company.
3. Change the number. The allowed range is shown under each field; a number outside it shows an error and Save stays disabled.
4. Click Save. The message «Policies saved» appears.
Change who may do what in comments
1. Scroll to «Who does what in task comments».
2. Each row is a relation to the task; each column is an action: read, write a comment, reply, upload a file, mention with @, edit own comment, delete own comment.
3. Tick or untick the boxes and click Save. The change applies at once, including to old comments.

Fields (form inputs)
Company (top of the page)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Company | Whose policies you see and change; each company has its own numbers. | Yes | One of the companies you may reach.
Policy numbers (one form, saved all at once with Save; the range is shown under each field)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Urgent when due within (days) | A task due within this many days gets the «Urgent» mark and counts as urgent in the matrix. | Yes | Whole number 0 to 14 (default 2).
Reminder before the due date (days) | How many days before the due date the assignee gets the reminder. | Yes | 1 to 7 (default 1).
Back-dating allowed (days) | How far back a completion date or a logged working day may go; also the late-completion limit. | Yes | 0 to 30 (default 7).
Stale after no movement for (days) | A task with no movement for this long gets the «Stale» mark. | Yes | 7 to 180 (default 30).
An objection lapses after (working days) | How long an objection waits for an answer before it lapses (Friday and Saturday are off). | Yes | 1 to 10 (default 3).
Day of the managers' summary (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday) | The weekday when each manager gets the overdue summary of their team. | Yes | 0 to 6 (default 0).
Archive standalone tasks after closing (days) | How long a closed standalone task stays in the lists before it is archived. | Yes | 7 to 365 (default 30).
Most files in a comment | The most files one comment may carry. | Yes | 1 to 10 (default 5).
Time to edit or delete a comment (minutes) | How long the author may edit or delete their own comment. | Yes | 0 to 1440 (default 15).
Close the conversation after the task is done (days, 0 = never) | Days after the task closes when its conversation becomes read-only. | Yes | 0 to 365 (default 0 = never).
Who does what in task comments (a table of boxes, saved all at once; shown with View the comment rules matrix, changed with Edit the comment rules matrix)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
A box for each relation and action | Rows: Assignee, Who gave the task, Responsible (approver), Reviewer, Follower, Manager (within their team's reach), Colleague with an open task of the same category, Mentioned with @. Columns: Read, Write, Reply, Upload a file, Mention @, Edit own, Delete own. A ticked box lets people with that relation do that action, if their role also holds the action's key. | Every box is saved (ticked or not) | Ticked / unticked. Starting point: the first six relations may do everything; the colleague and the mentioned person may only read, write and reply.

Workflow
A policy has no approval steps: it is changed and applies. What matters is what each number does afterwards.
1. An administrator turns on platform admin mode and opens Task policies.
2. Chooses the company, changes the numbers (each is checked against its range; Save stays disabled while one is empty or outside it) and clicks Save. «Policies saved» appears.
3. The new numbers apply to the next check: marks (urgent, stale) are worked out from them every time a list is read; reminders, overdue notices, archiving and objection time use them in the next run; back-dating and comment limits apply to the next action.
4. In the comments table the administrator ticks or unticks boxes and clicks Save; the change applies at once, to old comments too.
5. A company that was never saved works with the defaults above.
Status | Meaning | Who can move it (permission key) | Moves to
Defaults | The company has not saved its own numbers. | — | Saved by the company.
Saved by the company | The numbers (and the comments table) the administrator saved. | Edit the task policies for the numbers; Edit the comment rules matrix for the table. | Saved again with other values.
Automatic things: the numbers drive the daily job at 6:00 (reminders, overdue notices, archiving), the managers' summary at 8:00 on the chosen weekday, the scheduled lapse of an objection, the «Stale» and «Urgent» marks, and the comment limits. Every policy change is recorded in the audit log.
What each person sees: only people with View the task policies page (platform administrators, in admin mode) see the page. Ordinary people never see the numbers; they feel them as the reminders, marks and limits they meet. The comments table appears only with View the comment rules matrix, and its boxes can be changed only with Edit the comment rules matrix.

Business rules
- The numbers, their default values and their limits (FR-54, FR-66):
Number | Default | Allowed
Urgent if due within (days) | 2 | 0 to 14
Reminder before due date (days) | 1 | 1 to 7
Back-dating allowed (days) | 7 | 0 to 30
Stale after no movement (days) | 30 | 7 to 180
An objection lapses after (working days) | 3 | 1 to 10
Managers' digest day (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday) | 0 | 0 to 6
Archive standalone tasks after closing (days) | 30 | 7 to 365
Most files in a comment | 5 | 1 to 10
Time to edit or delete a comment (minutes) | 15 | 0 to 1440
Close the conversation after the task is done (days, 0 = never) | 0 | 0 to 365
- Policies are per company; each company has its own numbers.
- Working days exclude Friday and Saturday.
- A policy change is recorded in the audit log.
- The conversation table: a row for each relation (the assignee, the person who gave the task, the responsible approver, the reviewer, the follower, the manager inside the team's scope, a colleague with an open task in the same category, a person mentioned with @). An action passes when the person's role holds its key and a box is ticked for one of their relations.
- By default the first six relations may do everything. The colleague and the mentioned person (marked with *) may only read, write and reply; they see only the task number, title and conversation.
- A company starts with these defaults until someone changes them.

Tips / common problems
- The page is not in the menu: turn on platform admin mode, or you lack View the task policies page.
- Save is disabled: one of the numbers is empty or outside its range.
- A person says they cannot comment: check both their role keys and their relation row in the conversation table.

title: Tickets
text:
A ticket is the official way to ask another department for something: you choose the department and the kind of request, write what you need, and follow the replies until the ticket is closed. Each ticket has a number such as TKT-000123. The list can be shown as a table, as cards, or as a board with one column per status.

Who sees it
- View permission: View the tickets page and ticket details («View the tickets page and ticket details»). Default scope: own, meaning the tickets you sent or that are handled by you.
- Default roles: the Employee role holds view (own), send a ticket, reply (own), ask to close, confirm or reject closing, close without execution, reopen, and the reply and mention keys. The head role of each unit holds view, reply and reassign at «unit and below», and export.
- No platform admin mode is needed.
- A ticket outside your relation or scope is shown as «not found». Attachments can be downloaded only by people who may see the ticket.

What you can do
Action | What happens | Permission
New ticket | Opens the two-step popup to send a ticket | Send a new ticket
Open a ticket | Click the row, or the eye icon, to open its page | View the tickets page and ticket details
Report a problem | The bug button («Report a problem») in the top bar of every page (shown while the administrator has reports on): takes a screenshot of the screen, asks for a line about the problem, and sends it as a ticket of the type the administrator chose; see «Reporting a problem in the platform» below | Report a problem in the platform (a screenshot and a ticket) (Report a problem in the platform; every role holds it by default)
Reply | Writes an answer with files and mentions | Reply to and handle tickets (ask to close, close without executing) (Reply to and handle tickets)
Answer a reply | Replies to one reply, one level only | Answer a reply inside a ticket
Mention with @ | Names a colleague in a reply | Mention a colleague with @ in a ticket reply
Request closing | The unit side asks the sender to confirm it was done | Ask to close a ticket
Confirm it was done | The sender confirms and the ticket is closed | Approve the closing of a ticket
Not done yet | The sender rejects the closing; the ticket returns to the department | Reject the closing of a ticket
Send the reply and confirm the closing | In the reply box of a ticket waiting for your confirmation: sends your reply and closes the ticket in one step (a plain «Send the reply» returns the ticket to «open», as a note under the box says) | Reply to and handle tickets (ask to close, close without executing) (Reply to and handle tickets) and Approve the closing of a ticket, both
Close without carrying out | The department closes it, explaining why | Close a ticket without executing it
Reopen | The sender reopens a closed ticket within the allowed days | Reopen a closed ticket
Delete | Hides a ticket and its replies from everyone after a confirmation (any status); the record stays in the database and the audit log says who deleted it. Shown as a trash icon on the row of the list and as a button on the ticket's page, where your scope reaches the ticket's department; with the key at the narrowest scope («own») you delete only the tickets you sent | Delete a ticket (hidden from everyone, its record is kept); «own» = only the tickets the person sent (Delete a ticket); not held by the «Employee» role, held by the head role of every unit for its unit and below
Choose handler | On a ticket whose type has several handlers and that nobody has taken, the unit head picks one of that type's handlers; the ticket becomes theirs, they are notified, and it disappears from the other handlers | Choose who answers a ticket among the handlers of its type
Reassign | A unit head hands an open ticket of their unit to someone on their team | Reassign a ticket to another employee
Quick reply | On the board, a short reply from the card | Reply to and handle tickets (ask to close, close without executing)
Export | The «Export» button of the list's toolbar: choose the scope (the tickets on this page, or all the results of the tab, search and filters you have on), the columns and the file type (Excel, CSV). The file holds the number, title, the ticket's text, department, type, sender, handler, status, priority, needed-by date, send date and last activity. You export only the tickets you can see, never more | Export the ticket list (only the tickets the person sees) (Export the ticket list); not held by the «Employee» role, held by the head role of every unit
The tickets list has no import button. Tickets are sent one by one from the popup, not from a file.

How to
Send a ticket
1. Click New ticket.
2. Step 1: type in «What do you need?», or narrow by department and kind (regular or personal). Choose the view «By department» or «Compact list». Click the kind you want.
3. Step 2: write the title (required) and the details, choose the needed-by date, mark the ticket urgent if needed, and attach up to 5 files.
4. Press Send (or Ctrl+Enter). The message «The ticket was sent» appears and the ticket gets its number.
Answer a ticket you handle
1. Open the Unit inbox tab and click the ticket.
2. Write in «Your reply», attach files if needed, and click Send reply.
3. When the work is done, click Request closing and add an optional message.
Close a ticket you sent
1. Open the ticket. If the department asked to close, you see Confirm it was done and Not done yet.
2. Click Confirm it was done to close it, or Not done yet to send it back open with your message.
3. If the ticket is closed and you still need it, click Reopen (the page shows how many days are left).
Choosing the handler (unit heads): when a ticket's type has several handlers and nobody has taken it (their names show under «Responsible») the Choose handler button appears for whoever holds the key and whose reach includes the ticket's unit. You can pick only one of the type's handlers: the ticket moves to them, they are notified, and it disappears from the other handlers' lists, who can no longer open or answer it. Likewise whoever answers first, before any choice, takes the ticket and it disappears from the rest. The head of every unit holds the key automatically for their unit and below.
Reassigning (unit heads): on an open ticket of your unit click Reassign, search a name or number, and choose the person. Only people inside your own unit and the units below it appear. The ticket moves to them, they are notified, and the history shows who handed it to whom.
Find tickets
1. Use the search box (title, details or number) and the filters: unit, type, assignee, status.
2. Group by assignee, status, unit or type, and switch between table, board and cards.

Fields (form inputs)
New ticket, step 1: choose what you need
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
What do you need? | Search box over the types of every department. Type a few words («laptop», «certificate») and the matching types appear. | No | Free text; only narrows the list.
Department | Narrows the list to one department. The department decides who receives the ticket. | No | A department that receives tickets; «All units» shows all. Paused departments are shown disabled with the reason; stopped ones are not shown.
Kind of request | Regular requests or personal ones (complaints, private matters). | No | All kinds / Regular / Personal.
By department / Compact list | Only changes how the types are displayed. | No | Two views.
The type (click a card or row) | The kind of request. It fixes the department, the people who handle it (the type's handlers, otherwise the department manager), the usual duration, and whether the ticket is personal. | Yes | An active type of an available department.
New ticket, step 2: the ticket
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Instructions for this type (read-only box above the fields) | What the unit asks you to include in a ticket of this type so it is easy to answer (for example, a screenshot of the problem). Read it before you write; it appears only when the type has instructions and never blocks sending. | No | Formatted text written by the unit leader.
Title | A short line the handler reads first and the list shows. | Yes | 1 to 200 characters. Message when empty: «Write a title for the ticket.»
Details | The full request: what you need, and everything the handler needs to act without asking again. | No | Up to 5000 characters.
When do you need it | The needed-by date. It drives the «Overdue» mark once it passes. | Yes | A date not earlier than today plus the department's minimum lead in working days; otherwise «The earliest date this unit accepts is …». It is pre-filled with today plus the type's usual time (or the department's) in working days.
Priority | Marks the ticket as «Urgent»; the mark shows in lists and on the board so the handler sees it first. | No | Switch: Normal (default) or On.
Ticket attachments | Files that support the request (drag them in or click to browse). | No | Up to 5 files, each up to the size the administrator set (10 MB until changed); Word, Excel, PowerPoint, images, PDF and CSV. Each chosen file shows as a thumbnail (a picture) or a file icon: click it to open it full size and check it before sending. The files must be your own uploads.
Pressing Change at the top of step 2 returns to step 1 without losing what you typed. The sender and the department are never typed: they come from you and from the chosen type.
Reply box (on the ticket page, and «Quick reply» on the board)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Your reply | The text of your answer; the other side is notified (by number and department only, never the text). | Yes | 1 to 5000 characters. Type @ to mention a colleague (needs Mention a colleague with @ in a ticket reply): the person is notified, also by e-mail.
Mention (@) | Brings a colleague into the conversation. A mentioned person can read and answer, nothing more. | No | Active employees of the ticket's company. In a personal ticket only the sender and the assignee.
Answer this reply | Answers one earlier reply (needs Answer a reply inside a ticket); the person you answer is notified. | No | One level only: an answer to an answer is filed under the first reply.
Ticket attachments | Files with the reply. | No | Up to 5 files.
Message box of the close actions (Request closing, Confirm it was done, Not done yet, Close without carrying out, Reopen)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Message (optional) | A note kept in the ticket history and sent with the action: what was done, why it was not done, why you reopen. | No | Up to 5000 characters.

Reporting a problem in the platform
Something does not work? Press the bug button («Report a problem») in the top bar, or the same button beside the «Close» button of any pop-up window that is open (a pop-up covers the top bar), so a problem inside a pop-up can be reported with the pop-up in the screenshot (it appears only while the administrator has «Report a problem» switched on in Settings → Problem reports).
1. A screenshot of what the window shows is taken from the page itself (no permission to give). Password fields are left out.
2. A window shows the screenshot (click it to see it full size), a box What is the problem? (optional, up to 1000 characters) and a line saying what goes with the report: the page name, the browser, the window size, the language, the theme and the last errors; the content of the page is not sent, only the screenshot.
3. Report title (optional; empty = the page's name) and What is the problem? are yours to write. Press Analyse with the AI (it appears when the administrator switched the analysis on and an AI service is on) and the AI writes the title and the description for you from your note, the page details and, only if the administrator allowed it, the screenshot; read them and change what you want before sending. Nothing is analysed unless you press the button.
4. Untick Attach the screenshot to send the report as text alone. If the administrator allowed the AI service to see screenshots, a warning says so while the box is ticked.
5. Send the report. A ticket of the chosen type is made in your name: you follow its replies in «My tickets» like any ticket, and the department's handlers receive it in their unit inbox. A notice gives its number with a button to open it.
6. If the AI is off or fails when you press its button, a message says so and you write the description yourself; sending never depends on it.
Rule | Value
Who may report | Whoever holds Report a problem in the platform (a screenshot and a ticket)
Limit | The number of reports an hour the administrator set (default 10, 1 to 60); past it, wait a little
Refused | While the button is off or the chosen type is no longer usable; with a screenshot that is not yours
The administrator sets all of this in Settings → Problem reports (see the Settings page).

Workflow
What happens when someone raises a ticket
1. The sender clicks New ticket, chooses the type, writes the title and details, picks the needed-by date, marks it urgent if needed, attaches files and presses Send. The system checks that the department is receiving (active, started, with a manager), that the date is not too early, and that the files are the sender's own.
2. The ticket gets its number (TKT-000123), status Open, and appears in the sender's «My tickets» tab. The history gets the entry «The ticket was sent». (On the ticket page «Conversation and replies» holds the replies and the message written with a step (closing requested, «Not done yet», closed without being carried out, reopened), headed with the step, so the sender reads the closing message there; every other step is in the History of the ticket section at the bottom: the View history button opens a window with a table: number, date and time, by, event and details: the message that came with it, the files and the person the ticket was handed to.)
3. The handlers are told (in the app and by e-mail): the type's handler, or all of them when it has several (the ticket then has no assignee yet, shows in every handler's «Unit inbox», and the first one to reply becomes its assignee), or the department manager when the type has no handler. The notice carries only the number and the department. The ticket appears in the handler's «Unit inbox» tab with the mark «New» until somebody from the unit answers.
4. The handler (the assignee, the department manager, or someone whose reply scope reaches the department) opens the ticket and answers with Send reply. The first answer from the unit's side records the first response time. The sender is notified of each reply and answers in the same way (Reply to and handle tickets (ask to close, close without executing)).
5. When the work is done the handler clicks Request closing and may add a message. The status becomes Waiting for closing confirmation, the sender is notified (also by e-mail, with the number and the department only), your message appears in the sender's Conversation and replies headed «Closing of the ticket was requested», and the clock for automatic closing starts.
6. The sender chooses one:
   - Confirm it was done: the ticket closes («confirmed by the sender»).
   - Not done yet: the ticket returns to Open with the sender's message, and the unit is notified.
   - Writes a reply with «Send the reply»: the ticket also returns to Open and the closing request is cancelled. With «Send the reply and confirm the closing» the reply is sent and the ticket is closed (confirmed by the sender) in one step; it works even for a sender who also manages the receiving department.
   - Does nothing: after the department's automatic-close days the system closes it («automatically») and tells both sides.
1. If the unit cannot or will not carry out the request, the handler clicks Close without carrying out with the reason; the sender is notified.
2. After closing the sender may click Reopen during the department's reopen window (the page shows the days left). The ticket returns to Open and the unit is notified.
Status | Meaning | Who can move it (permission key) | Moves to
Open | The ticket is with the unit, being handled | The unit side (assignee, department manager, or reply scope): Ask to close a ticket, Close a ticket without executing it | Waiting for closing confirmation; Closed (without being carried out)
Waiting for closing confirmation | The unit says it is done and waits for the sender | The sender: Approve the closing of a ticket, Reject the closing of a ticket, or a reply. The unit side: Close a ticket without executing it. The system: automatic close | Closed (confirmed by the sender); Open; Closed (without being carried out); Closed (automatically)
Closed | Finished: «confirmed by the sender», «automatically» or «without being carried out». It takes no new replies | The sender: Reopen a closed ticket, only inside the reopen window | Open
Replying never changes the status by itself, except a sender's reply while the ticket waits for closing confirmation (it returns to Open).
Automatic things
- Automatic closing: a durable timer starts when closing is requested and ends after the department's automatic-close days (default 4, calendar days). It does nothing if the ticket moved on meanwhile, and it is cancelled by any other change.
- Stale notice: every morning at 06:00 (Riyadh time) the system tells the unit (assignee, and the manager unless the ticket is personal) about open tickets with no activity for the department's stale days (default 14), once per quiet period. The «Overdue» and «Stale» marks are computed on the screen from the needed-by date and the last activity.
- Notifications: sending (to the handler, with e-mail), replies, mentions (with e-mail), answers to a reply, closing request (to the sender, with e-mail), close without carrying out, reopening, decline of closing and automatic close (both sides, with e-mail). Confirming closes silently. Nobody is notified of their own action.
- Audit: every step is recorded in the audit log (sent, replied, close requested, declined, confirmed, auto-closed, closed without execution, reopened).
- Concurrency: if two people act on the same ticket at once, the second action is refused and must be repeated.
What each person sees
- The sender sees the tickets they sent in «My tickets», with the full conversation and the buttons that fit the status (reply, confirm, not done yet, reopen).
- The handler sees the tickets assigned to them, or those of the department they manage or whose reply scope they hold, in «Unit inbox».
- The unit head (with the head role at «unit and below») sees and answers the tickets of the unit and below, and the people's tickets in «My team». A personal ticket is seen only by its sender and its assignee, not by the head or by platform administrators merely because of that role (a head who is the sender or the assignee sees it as such).

Business rules
- Tabs: My tickets (tickets I sent), Unit inbox (tickets assigned to me, or to my department if I manage it, or by my reply scope), My team's tickets (those of the people in my view scope). A tab appears only if you have something in it. (FR-38)
- Statuses: Open, Waiting for closing confirmation, Closed. A closed ticket shows how it ended: by sender's confirmation, automatically, or without execution. Marks: urgent, overdue, stale, new (nobody answered yet), personal.
- A ticket cannot be edited after it is sent. The conversation continues with replies until closing.
- Sending is refused when the department's reception is paused or stopped, when it has not started yet, or when it has no manager. A department that is stopped is not offered at all. (FR-37)
- The needed-by date cannot be earlier than the department's minimum lead time; the form tells you the earliest date.
- Life cycle: (FR-39)
Action | From | To | Who
Request closing | Open | Waiting for closing confirmation | the unit side (assignee, department manager, or whoever handles the department by reply scope)
Confirm it was done | Waiting for confirmation | Closed (confirmed) | the sender
Not done yet | Waiting for confirmation | Open | the sender
Sender replies | Waiting for confirmation | Open | the sender
Close without carrying out | Open or waiting | Closed (not executed) | the unit side
Automatic close | Waiting for confirmation | Closed (automatic) | the system, after the desk's days with no answer
Reopen | Closed | Open | the sender, within the reopen days
- Default durations of a department: usual completion 3 working days, automatic close 4 days after the close request, reopen window 7 days, stale after 14 days. Each department can change them (see Ticket setup). Working days exclude Friday and Saturday. Only the usual completion time and the earliest date are counted in working days; automatic close, the reopen window and the stale period are calendar days. (FR-41)
- Personal tickets (complaints and personal matters) go straight to the person assigned to that type. They are hidden from the unit manager and from platform administrators; the figures count them but never list them. (FR-38)
- Replies: up to 5 files each, text up to 5000 characters, one level of answers to a reply. In a personal ticket only the sender and the assignee can be mentioned. Previews open for images, PDF, Word, Excel and CSV (a CSV is drawn as a table, in UTF-8 or Excel's Arabic encoding).
- Notices (in the app, and by e-mail for important ones) carry only the ticket number and the department, never its text. The person you mention is told, and so is the person whose reply you answer. (FR-39)
- Two people changing a ticket at the same moment: the second action is refused and must be repeated.

Tips / common problems
- You cannot find the department you want: it may be paused, stopped, not started, or without a manager.
- You see no «Unit inbox» tab: no tickets are assigned to you or your department.
- The «Reopen» button vanished: the reopen days are over; send a new ticket.

title: Ticket setup
text:
Here the leader of a unit decides whether the unit receives tickets, what the sender reads about it, which kinds of ticket it takes, who handles each kind, and how long each step may take. Any unit of the organization structure (sector, department, section, unit, office) can be a ticket desk.

Who sees it
- View permission: View the ticket setup page («View the ticket setup page»). Scopes: own (the units you lead and every unit below), unit, unit and below, company, all.
- Needs platform admin mode: yes. Without it the page only says that admin mode must be turned on.
- Default roles: the head role created automatically for every unit holds the setup keys at «unit and below». Ordinary employees do not.
- You see only the units inside your scope; a person with scope «all» sees every unit.

What you can do
Action | What happens | Permission
Choose the unit | Shows the setup of that unit (a tree picker, with search) | View the ticket setup page
Change reception, descriptions, durations and Save | Saves the unit's settings | Edit a unit's reception and durations
Add type | Opens a popup for a new kind of ticket | Add a ticket type
Edit type (pencil icon) | Changes a type | Edit a ticket type
Delete type (bin icon) | Deletes or deactivates a type | Delete a ticket type
The page has two tabs: Settings and Types.

How to
Switch on a desk
1. Turn on platform admin mode and open Ticket setup.
2. Choose the unit. Under the picker you see «Manager: …»; if there is none, set it first: click the «Assign the unit manager in the structure» link under the reception status field (shown to who holds Assign unit leaders and acting leaders; until a manager is set, the «Active» choice is disabled with the reason shown); it opens in a new page on this very unit with the «Assign a leader or acting leader» form already open (needs Assign unit leaders and acting leaders and platform admin mode); choose the employee and save, then go back to the setup page, which stays as you left it.
3. In Settings, set the reception status to «Active» and write the description the sender will read (Arabic and English).
4. Set the durations and click Save.
Add a ticket type
1. Open the Types tab and click Add type.
2. Write the name and the description (Arabic and English).
3. Choose the handlers: one or more people from the unit manager and the employees of the unit and of the units below it (any title) who answer tickets of this kind. Leave it empty and the unit manager handles them. In Instructions write what the sender must include (for example: take a screenshot of the problem and one of Inspect); the sender sees it before sending.
4. Optionally set a special duration in working days; leave it empty to use the unit's usual duration.
5. Tick «Personal type» if the type is for complaints or private matters; a personal type must have exactly one handler. Keep «Active type» ticked and save.
Pause reception
1. In Settings choose «Paused» (the unit shows as disabled with a message, and you resume it by hand) or «Stopped» (the unit is not shown to anyone).
2. Save. Tickets already open continue to be handled as usual.

Fields (form inputs)
Unit picker
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Unit | The unit whose setup you want to see or change. Under it you read «Manager: …». | Yes | A unit inside your scope (tree picker with search). A unit without a manager shows «This unit has no manager yet: assign one in the organization structure to activate it.»
Settings tab: reception
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Reception status | Decides whether employees can send tickets to the unit now. | Yes | «Active» (listed and receives tickets), «Paused for now» (listed but disabled with a message; you resume it by hand), «Stopped» (not listed for anyone). Existing tickets are handled as usual in every state. A unit without a manager cannot be set to Active.
Accepts personal requests (the unit manager does not see them) | Lets the unit take personal types (complaints, private matters). | No | Tick box. Without it, personal types of this unit are refused.
Unit description for the sender (Arabic) / (English) | The sentence the employee reads when choosing this unit: what the unit does and what to send it. | No | Up to 500 characters each. The English one is filled from the Arabic when left empty.
Settings tab: durations (each a whole number of days, with its limits shown under the field)
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Usual completion time | The time the unit normally needs. It pre-fills the sender's needed-by date and is shown to senders. In working days (Friday and Saturday are off). | Yes | 1 to 60; default 3. A type may override it.
Earliest date that can be asked for | The minimum lead: a sender cannot ask for a date earlier than today plus this. In working days. | Yes | 0 to 30; default 0.
Automatic closing after a closing request | Days after «Request closing» when the system closes the ticket if the sender has not answered. In calendar days. | Yes | 1 to 30; default 4.
Time allowed for reopening | Days after closing during which the sender may reopen. In calendar days. | Yes | 1 to 60; default 7.
A ticket is stale after | Days without any activity on an open ticket before it is marked «Stale» and the unit is reminded. In calendar days. | Yes | 1 to 90; default 14.
Types tab: Add type / Edit the type
Field | What it means / what to type | Required | Allowed values / rules
Name in Arabic / Name in English | The name of the kind of request, shown to the employee when they send. | Yes | 2 to 120 characters each. The English one is filled from the Arabic when left empty.
Description in Arabic / in English | One line telling the employee when to choose this type. | No | Up to 300 characters each.
Handlers | The employees who answer tickets of this type and are notified when one arrives. One handler: the ticket is assigned to them. Several: the ticket shows to all and the first to reply takes it. Empty means the unit manager handles them. | Only for a personal type (exactly one) | Active employees of the unit and of every unit below it, any title, and the unit manager.
